# fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore (Resource)

Restores a VM from a Backup Native restore point. Applying the resource runs the restore once and waits for it to finish. Destroying it only removes it from state; it never changes the VM. Change a value in `triggers` to run the restore again. `overwrite` restores onto the original VM; `keep` creates a new VM and keeps the original. The API does not return the new VM's id; find it by `instance_name` with the `fptcloud_instances` data source. Run one restore per VM at a time; two concurrent restores of the same VM can be matched to the wrong history row. Once the restore has been sent, the resource is saved whatever the outcome, and the next apply does not restore again. A failed restore, a timeout or an interrupted apply (Ctrl+C) ends the apply with a warning, not an error, and stores the outcome in `status` and `message`. The restore goes on without Terraform after a timeout or an interrupt; each later plan or apply reads the restore history and stores the outcome once the restore ends. A restore that timed out before its history row appeared is matched to the first restore of the same source after it was sent. Only interrupt an apply once: a second Ctrl+C stops Terraform before it saves the restore, and the next apply restores again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore_points" "web" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  vm_id  = var.web_instance_id
}

# Restore the latest restore point into a new VM and keep the original.
# Any triggers value works and a new value restores again. A request time, as
# below, is recommended so the state records when each restore was requested.
resource "fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore" "web_copy" {
  vpc_id                   = var.vpc_id
  vm_id                    = var.web_instance_id
  restore_point_created_at = data.fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore_points.web.restore_points[0].created_at
  mode                     = "keep"

  instance_name      = "web-restored"
  flavor_id          = var.flavor_id
  subnet_id          = var.subnet_id
  security_group_ids = [var.security_group_id]

  triggers = { restore = "2026-10-26 09:00:00" }
}

# Find the new VM by name.
data "fptcloud_instances" "all" {
  vpc_id     = var.vpc_id
  depends_on = [fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore.web_copy]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `mode` (String) `overwrite` restores onto the original VM. `keep` creates a new VM and keeps the original.
- `restore_point_created_at` (String) `created_at` of the restore point, copied from `fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore_points`. The backend picks the restore point closest to this time within 10 minutes.
- `vm_id` (String) ID of the VM the restore point belongs to.
- `vpc_id` (String) ID of the VPC.

### Optional

- `flavor_id` (String) `keep` only, required for `keep`. ID of the new VM's flavor.
- `floating_ip` (String) `keep` only. Omit for no floating IP, `new` to allocate one, or the ID of a floating IP that is not in use.
- `instance_name` (String) `keep` only. Name of the new VM, at most 50 characters.
- `new_password` (String, Sensitive) New password for the restored VM.
- `power_on` (Boolean) Whether the restored VM is powered on.
- `private_ip` (String) `keep` only. Private IP of the new VM.
- `security_group_ids` (List of String) `keep` only. IDs of security groups for the new VM.
- `subnet_id` (String) `keep` only, required for `keep`. ID of the subnet (the `id` of `fptcloud_subnet`).
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values that run the restore again when they change, which no other argument can express because every other argument stays equal. Any string works; only a change matters. We recommend the time you ask for the action, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, for example `2026-10-26 09:00:00`, so the state records when each one was requested. Avoid `timestamp()`: it changes on every plan and repeats the action on every apply.

### Read-Only

- `finished_at` (String) End of the restore, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `message` (String) Why the action did not succeed, or why the provider stopped waiting for it. Empty after a success.
- `started_at` (String) Start of the restore, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `status` (String) Result of the restore: the status of its history row once it ended, `Success` or `Failed`. The provider stores its own value when the API has none to give: `tf_timeout` when the provider stopped waiting before the action ended, `tf_interrupted` when the apply was interrupted while it waited, `tf_failed` when the action failed without an API status. A plan or apply checks `tf_timeout` and `tf_interrupted` again and replaces them with the API's status once the action ends.
